recordedFrom.note: The runner prints its result to stdout and writes nothing durable. This bundle is that stdout object, verbatim; the path it was captured at is gitignored and will not survive. The first attempt at `.tmp/mpf-run.log` came back `blocked` with `move_placed_furniture_not_accepted` because the furniture was still on the carried-slot tile; this is the rerun that cleared it, and the blocked run is not evidence.

whatThisProves: The Mod really ran the game's own `GameLocation.removeQueuedFurniture` on the game thread: the receipt is `succeeded/placed_furniture_picked_up`, and the runner asserts that terminal before this object is printed.
The world moved, in the game's words: `removed_from_furniture=true` and `furniture_in_location` 9 -> 8, so the piece left the location's furniture list.
The piece arrived in the backpack: `carried=true`, `inventory_before=0` -> `inventory_after=1`, `(F)2048` held at `carried_tile=9,8` with rotation 0 and not flipped.
The game narrated it (`nativeNotices: [床]`, the piece's own display name), and revision advanced 0 -> 1 with no `activeExecution` left behind.
whatThisDoesNotProve: No cancellation, deadline, watchdog, replay or migration coverage.
Only pickup. The placement half of the intent is `place_owned_object`, which is a separate live_verified action.
No shared-world coverage. The seam is mp-insensitive per the derived multiplayer sensitivity register, so single-player native-local is the topology this action requires.
